name: What should I check first before installing a curbless shower?

mainEntity.name: What should I check first before installing a curbless shower?

acceptedAnswer.text:
A curbless shower can often be installed during a bathroom remodel, but the first step is confirming the existing floor structure, drain location, and available height. Elite Remodeling & Design can review the room during consultation and coordinate layout, design, plumbing, construction, and inspection needs as one project plan.

A zero-threshold entry is not created simply by removing a curb. The shower floor must slope toward the drain while the surrounding bathroom floor remains protected from water.

Key factors:
- Wood framing may need a carefully planned recess; slab floors may require different drain and floor solutions.
- Existing plumbing, joist direction, doorway height, and bathroom size affect feasibility.
- A linear drain, center drain, or other drainage layout may change the tile and slope design.

Before requesting a proposal, gather room dimensions, photos below the floor if available, and your preferred shower opening and fixture locations. Ask how the proposed design will manage slope, waterproofing, and transitions.

Elite Remodeling & Design can incorporate the shower into a broader bathroom remodeling plan rather than treating the entry as an isolated fixture change.
acceptedAnswer.description: Check the floor structure, drain location, available height, doorway transition, and waterproofing plan first. Removing a curb alone does not create a reliable zero-threshold shower. Elite Remodeling & Design can review these conditions during the bathroom design and construction planning stage.
